knowledge_point.title: Integrating Products Containing Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 x^{3} - \frac{\pi}{6}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6 x^{2}.
$$

Change both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{6^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{6}\\x=\frac{3^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{5} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{6^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}}^{\frac{3^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{5} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}} - 5 x^{2} \tan{\left(2 x^{3} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} \sec{\left(2 x^{3} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{5}{6}\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate and evaluate at both bounds:

$$
\left[- \frac{5 \sec{\left(u \right)}}{6}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=\left(- \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{6}\right)-\left(- \frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{9}\right).
$$

Simplifying gives

$$
- \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{6} + \frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{9}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Integrating Products Containing Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 \sqrt{x} - \frac{\pi}{6}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int - \frac{2 \cos{\left(2 \sqrt{x} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=-2\left(\int \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
-2\left(\int \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=- 2 \sin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
- 2 \sin{\left(2 \sqrt{x} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}+C.
$$
